newsitem.title: GERMANY: European Patent office lowers fees 20 percent.
newsitem.headline: European Patent office lowers fees 20 percent.

text.p: The European Patent Office (EPO) will next year lower fees for obtaining patents on average by about 20 percent, the Munich-based organization said on Monday.
As of July 1, 1997, a patent covering eight of the group's 18 member countries will cost 8,900 marks, instead of 11,050 marks, EPO president Ingo Kober said.
The EPO may further reduce fees later as it streamlines the rules for translating patents, which accounts for 37 percent of the application costs, Kober said.
Kober has proposed requiring only translations of patent summaries, rather than precise legal documents in the languages used by member states.
Without such a change, translation costs would skyrocket after the EPO's planned expansion to 30 members in the next four years, Kober said.
